name: Visual Basic 16
title: Visual Basic 16 (.NET)

type.text: **`Option Strict Off` is the default**: Under it an implicit narrowing conversion and a late-bound `Object` call compile, and the type is resolved when the statement runs
**`Option Strict On` removes the late-bound path**: The same code does not compile until the conversion or the reference is written explicitly
**`Interface` and `Implements` separate a contract from its implementation**: A class names the interface members it supplies
**A nullable value type states an absence**: `Integer?` is `Nullable(Of Integer)`, and `HasValue` and `Value` test and read it

**`Nothing` is compatible with every reference type**: A reference may be `Nothing`, no declaration requires a test before use, the language offers no nullable reference annotation, and for a string `"" = Nothing` is `True`
**A class hierarchy couples a derived class to its base**: `Inherits` binds a class to the base's virtual members, and an `Interface` with `Implements` is the alternative that avoids the chain

construction.text: **`Sub New` is a real constructor**: A class declares it, `Overloads` gives several signatures, and `MyBase.New` runs the base constructor
**`ReadOnly` and `Const` mark a fixed value**: A `ReadOnly` field is set once, and a `Const` is fixed at compile time
**Mutability is the default**: A `Dim` variable and a property are writable, and only an explicit `ReadOnly` or `Const` changes that
**A `Structure` is a value type with its own constructor**: A copy of a structure is a copy of its values, and it is not collected
**`Using` bounds the life of a resource**: The block calls `Dispose` on every exit path

**`WithEvents` binds the handler object to its source**: A `WithEvents` field is tied to the events of one declared type, and `Handles` lists the events it answers, so the subscription is written into the declaration

memory.text: **The garbage collector decides when memory returns**: A reference is reclaimed after it becomes unreachable, and a collection pause is possible
**No release runs at the end of a scope**: A class has a finalizer at best, whose time is not defined, and there is no deterministic destructor
**No ownership model**: A reference may alias, and nothing in the type states who releases the object
**`Using` gives deterministic release for an `IDisposable`**: The block calls `Dispose` on every exit, including the exceptional one
**`IDisposable` is the stated protocol for a native resource**: A type that holds a handle states its release method
**A finalizer delays the collection of its object**: The object survives one extra collection while the finalizer queue is drained

error.text: **The exceptions are unchecked**: No method signature states the exceptions it may raise, so a `Try` is a convention
**A failure can be discarded by design**: `On Error Resume Next` and an empty `Catch` both let a failure pass with no effect
**`Try`/`Catch`/`Finally` is a structured path**: The `Catch` block holds the recovery code and `Finally` runs on every exit
**The failure is selected by type**: `Catch ex As IOException` chooses by exception type, and `ex.InnerException` carries the cause
**The legacy `On Error GoTo` form remains**: It binds the recovery to a line label and a sequence, beside the structured form
**An `Async` failure arrives at the `Await`**: An exception in an awaited task surfaces at the await, so the `Try` block must span it

concurrency.text: **Synchronisation is manual with no race detection**: `SyncLock` guards a block, and the compiler analyses no program for a race
**`SyncLock` is a language construct**: It takes a lock on an expression and releases it at the end of the block
**`Async` and `Await` state the suspension point**: An asynchronous call reads as a sequence, and the language marks where it yields
**The task and thread types come from the runtime**: `Task`, `Thread`, and the thread pool are .NET types the language uses directly
**The lock order is not stated**: `SyncLock` names a lock and not an order, so a deadlock is a design concern outside the language
**An event handler runs on the raising thread**: An event raised on a worker thread runs the handler there, and the UI-thread rule is a framework convention
**`Thread` reserves an operating-system thread**: Each task holds one for its whole life

platform.text: **The compiler emits a portable .NET assembly**: The resulting `.dll` or `.exe` runs wherever the .NET runtime runs
**The runtime runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS**: The same assembly runs on each, so the language is not bound to one operating system
**The class library is reachable**: An assembly with a public surface can be consumed from Visual Basic
**The project system is the common one**: A `.vbproj` is an SDK-style project built by `dotnet build`

**A few newer features have no Visual Basic form**: Nullable reference annotations and static abstract interface members have no equivalent syntax, so a consumer of a library that requires them needs a wrapper
**Windows Forms and WPF target Windows only**: A GUI project on either framework runs on Windows

performance.text: **The compiler emits IL and the runtime compiles it**: The hot path becomes machine code through the just-in-time compiler
**The collector is generational**: A short-lived object is reclaimed cheaply
**The runtime library supplies the fast paths**: `StringBuilder` and the asynchronous I/O APIs are available to a Visual Basic program
**The first call of a method is the slowest**: Compilation happens on first use, so start-up includes a warm-up
**Boxing and string concatenation allocate**: An `Object`-typed value and a repeated `&` produce garbage on the heap
**A collection pause is possible on a large heap**: The collector's pause is outside the program's control

ecosystem.text: **NuGet is the package manager**: A dependency is declared in the project and restored by `dotnet restore`
**The IDE is Visual Studio**: Editing, refactoring, debugging, and the designer are integrated, and the free edition supports Visual Basic
**The class library is large and documented**: I/O, networking, collections, and UI are covered by the runtime
**The compiler ships with the platform**: `vbc` is maintained with the .NET SDK
**The published example is usually C#**: A library's documentation and samples are C#, and a Visual Basic consumer translates them
**New libraries are rarely written in Visual Basic**: The language's share of new code is small

evolution.text: **The language line is closed to new features**: Microsoft has stated that Visual Basic will not be evolved for new workloads, and the language receives no new syntax
**The language remains supported for existing code**: The compiler is maintained with the .NET SDK for bug fixes and platform compatibility
**The runtime advances under the language**: An existing assembly runs on a current .NET, so the platform moves even though the language does not
**A migration path to C# exists and is close**: The language improved substantially from Visual Basic 6, and the constructs and the object model map almost one to one onto C#
**A new framework feature can be C#-only**: Nullable reference types and static abstract interface members arrived without a Visual Basic form

domain.text: **Office and COM automation is a native domain**: `Object` and late binding make an Office object model usable without an interop assembly
**Windows Forms is the rapid-desktop domain**: The designer and the event model fit a business form application
**Console tools and services are straightforward**: A short program builds into an `.exe` in the .NET toolchain
**The .NET library ecosystem is reachable**: Any assembly with a public surface can be consumed
**Modern .NET UI frameworks are not offered for Visual Basic**: The .NET MAUI and Blazor templates are C#, so a new Visual Basic GUI is a Windows Forms or WPF project
**It is not the choice for new development**: The language remains less expressive than C# on the newer features, and the direction of the ecosystem is C#

learning.text: **The syntax is readable and close to English**: `If ... Then`, `For Each ... In`, and `End Sub` read as their meaning
**The curve is gentle from BASIC or Visual Basic 6**: The surface carries over, and the runtime supplies the rest
**The reference documentation is complete**: Microsoft documents every statement, keyword, and option
**The IDE guides a new user**: IntelliSense and the compiler's messages explain a construct as it is written
**Four `Option` statements change the language**: `Strict`, `Explicit`, `Infer`, and `Compare` each alter what compiles or what a comparison means
**The large subject is the class library**: The framework, not the syntax, is the bulk of the work

syntax.text: **The syntax is verbose**: Every block closes with its own keyword pair such as `End If`, `End Sub`, and `Next`, and a declaration repeats `Dim` and `As`
**Keywords are words**: The reading is close to English
**A line ends a statement**: Continuation is explicit with `_`
**Attributes are written in angle brackets**: `<Serializable>` and `<Obsolete("...")>` attach metadata to a declaration
**A file-level `Option` changes the parse**: `Option Strict On` at the top of a file changes which lines compile
**The language is case-insensitive**: `myValue` and `MyValue` name the same variable, so a rename is not caught by the case

testing.text: **A test framework is available from NuGet**: MSTest, NUnit, and xUnit all run against the .NET test SDK
**`dotnet test` runs the suite**: Discovery, execution, and the report come from the platform
**A test is written in Visual Basic**: Attributes such as `<TestMethod>` mark a test method
**The debugger is integrated**: A failed test can be stepped through in Visual Studio
**An assertion or mocking library is a package**: NUnit's assertions and Moq are consumed from NuGet
**The default `Option Strict Off` weakens the test itself**: A test project with the default setting can pass a value of a wrong type and notice only at run time

security.text: **The runtime is memory-safe**: No use-after-free and no buffer overrun occurs in safe code, and the language has no pointer type
**No `unsafe` context exists in Visual Basic**: The unverifiable memory operations of the runtime are out of reach
**The exception path keeps the failure in a value**: `ex.Message` and `ex.InnerException` carry the detail to a handler
**`Option Strict On` removes the late-bound call**: The member is resolved by the compiler rather than by name at run time
**`On Error Resume Next` can hide a failure that matters**: A suppressed failure leaves the program in a state the next statement does not expect
**A COM interop boundary is outside the runtime's checks**: A late-bound call crosses into unmanaged code that the type system does not verify

tradeoffs: **Late binding is the pragmatic COM path**: `Option Strict Off` around an Office object model avoids an interop reference, which is why the setting survives
**The Visual Basic 6 heritage is deliberate**: `On Error`, `My`, and the forms designer are continuity choices for the existing developer base
**Verbosity buys explicitness**: `End If` and `End Sub` are redundant, and the end of every block is visible
**The design-time form designer is a tool**: The layout is a tool feature rather than a language mechanism
**A port to C# is mechanical**: The constructs map closely, and the effort is the trade for leaving the language line
**A frozen language is stable for existing code**: No feature churn reaches a maintained program
verdict: Visual Basic .NET reaches a mid-range core score by inheriting the .NET runtime's separation of interface from implementation, its collected memory, and its checked types, while keeping the older Visual Basic defaults beside them. The losses are those defaults: `Option Strict Off`, a `Nothing` that fits every reference type, unchecked exceptions, a failure a caller may discard, and manual synchronisation. Main strengths: interfaces, `Option Strict On`, `Using` for deterministic release, the whole .NET class library, and a mechanical path to C#. Main weaknesses: `Option Strict Off` defers a conversion to run time, `Nothing` is not a checked absence, the collector decides when memory returns, a race has no detector, and the language line is closed to new features.

energy.text: Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Moderate training data: models write it competently, with measurable language-specific weakness [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
